title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
tasks_benchmarks: ImageNet-C (Gaussian noise sev. 3, contrast sev. 4) on 38,000 held-out ImageNet validation images

headline_result.text: Claude Opus 5.5-written weight programs raised SCAN exact match on new jump compositions from 0.0% to 99.8% by changing 257 weights, BabyAI pickup success from 0% to 98.4%, and ImageNet ResNet-18 net gains under corruption to 8.84-17.62 points versus 8.67 and 3.38 for the best of eight fine-tuning methods.
headline_result.quote: SCAN, add primitive grammar, 64 old 0.0% 99.8% 0.0 257 grammar-generated 99.6% 0.0

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: one LLM session per program; 10 ViT-Lite sessions over 3 seeds, 2 sessions per ImageNet condition; reruns on 5 independently trained networks

key_claims.claim: On ImageNet ResNet-18 under Gaussian noise, the first program reached a net gain of +10.47 points versus +8.67 for the best kept fine-tuning and +8.84 for the best fixed reference, changing 2,152,928 weights.
Eight demonstrations let a program add a pickup action to a BabyAI policy (0% to 98.4%) while behavior cloning on the same demonstrations reached 1.1%.
key_claims.quote: BabyAI, pick up 8 demonstrations, 64 old 0.0% 98.4% +0.4 21,482 behavior cloning, 1.1% −0.6

key_claims.claim: Rerunning a program without the LLM on five independently trained ViT-Lites keeps most of its gain, while copying the fixed weight edit gives almost nothing.
key_claims.quote: Rerunning the same program recomputes effective edits across independently trained networks, whereas copying its fixed weight edit does not reproduce the gain.

key_claims.claim: Access to weight values matters: the same LLM without weight values or network outputs reached +10.78 and +11.18 versus +31.75 and +17.98 with access.
A post hoc generic gated search without an LLM, written after reading the programs, reached +24.12 under Gaussian noise on the ViT-Lite.
key_claims.quote: generic gated search, no LLM +24.12 unchanged

notes_for_review: The largest and most controlled positive WSP study in the set: Claude Opus 5.5 writes Python programs that compute weight edits from weights, activations and a few labeled examples, compared against eight fine-tuning methods and eleven fixed references under matched data, checks and a clean-accuracy retention rule. Strengths are held-out test sets, causal ablations of the installed gates, a no-weights LLM control and reruns on independently trained networks; weaknesses are one LLM session per program, criteria fixed by the authors rather than preregistered, a counting rule set after reading two sessions, and a non-LLM gated search that recovers much of the ViT-Lite noise gain. The programs may run forward passes and use 8 labeled checks, so this is closer to LLM-written feature engineering with feedback than to weight reading alone.
